newsitem.title: UK: Londoners the worst money managers in Britain-poll.
newsitem.headline: Londoners the worst money managers in Britain-poll.

text.p: Londoners are the worst money managers in Britain, having lost track of more than 2,000 stg each, a study by the Independent Financial Adviser Promotion trade group said on Thursday.
The survey said the average Briton has lost track of 1,700 stg, while residents of the Midlands are the most conscientious in the country, keeping tabs on all but 1,400 stg of their money.
The report studied funds lying unclaimed in banks, building societies, savings schemes, unclaimed company benefits, the National Lottery and with bookmakers across Britain in 1996.
It said some 77 billion stg is currently lying "lost" or "forgotten" across the country.
Independent Financial Adviser Promotion is a body of financial advisers that commissioned the study as part of its "Save Smarter" campaign, to examine the need for professional money management.
